newsitem.title: GERMANY: Vereinsbank to announce share swap terms.
newsitem.headline: Vereinsbank to announce share swap terms.

text.p: Germany's Bayerische Vereinsbank said on Monday that it would announce on Thursday details of a swap of shares in insurer Allianz AG for shares in Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechselbank (Hypo-Bank).

The swap was preliminarily announced last week as part of a merger deal to integrate Hypo-Bank into Vereinsbank to create Germany's second-largest bank. Under the terms of that announcement, Hypo-Bank shareholders will receive one Allianz share for every six Hypo-Bank shares held.
The two banks said the details of the swap would be announced at a news conference to be held at 1100 GMT on Thursday in Munich.

"Board members of Vereinsbank and Hypo-Bank will present the construction and details of this swap transaction," the two banks said in the invitation. The invitation gave no additional information on the exchange.
The shares to be offered to Hypo-Bank shareholders will come from Vereinsbank's portfolio, according to information given when the merger was announced last week.
The swap plans have been lauded in Germany as a clever way to effect a merger while also freeing up hidden assets without attracting a high tax bill.

German banks have built up a large quantity of hidden assets as stock portfolios acquired over the years have gained in value. Although some have the stated objective of reducing these holdings, the tax levied on profits from a sale represent a huge disincentive to act.
